title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於是而無以制其外何以護厥中乎彼無稽之言
乃言之不合中道者聽之則必妨害於政治矣是
言也汝當勿聽之焉弗詢之謀乃謀之不合中道
者用之亦必妨害於政治矣是謀也汝當勿庸之
焉如是則內外相資而治道備矣苟守之而不以
敬何以保其治乎是故主乎民者君也可愛非君
乎統于君者民也可畏非民乎是何也蓋民非其
君雖有億兆之衆而無所奉戴此君之所以可愛
也君非其民雖有金湯之固而無與守邦此民之
===
所以可畏也君民相須如此今汝將為君而治民
也烏可以不敬哉必也戒謹恐懼而謹其在天子
之位不使一念一日之放肆有以貽大憂而召遠
患可也戰兢惕勵而脩其可願之善罔俾一毫一
事之不善生於心而害於政可也若然則謹位之
道盡而為君有可愛之實又何民之可畏哉致治
保治之道蓋至此而無以加矣嗟夫中者聖聖相
傳之心法而敬者又聖學之所以成始而成終者
也人君之治天下非中則致治之本不立非敬則
punctuated: 於是而無以制其外，何以護厥中乎？彼無稽之言，乃言之不合中道者，聽之則必妨害於政治矣。是言也，汝當勿聽之焉。弗詢之謀，乃謀之不合中道者，用之亦必妨害於政治矣。是謀也，汝當勿庸之焉。如是則內外相資，而治道備矣。苟守之而不以敬，何以保其治乎？是故主乎民者君也，可愛非君乎？統于君者民也，可畏非民乎？是何也？蓋民非其君，雖有億兆之衆而無所奉戴，此君之所以可愛也；君非其民，雖有金湯之固而無與守邦，此民之所以可畏也。君民相須如此，今汝將為君而治民也，烏可以不敬哉？必也戒謹恐懼，而謹其在天子之位，不使一念一日之放肆，有以貽大憂而召遠患，可也；戰兢惕勵，而脩其可願之善，罔俾一毫一事之不善，生於心而害於政，可也。若然，則謹位之道盡，而為君有可愛之實，又何民之可畏哉？致治保治之道，蓋至此而無以加矣。」嗟夫！中者，聖聖相傳之心法；而敬者，又聖學之所以成始而成終者也。人君之治天下，非中則致治之本不立，非敬則
translation_en: … at this point there is no means to regulate what is external, how can one protect that Mean within? Those unfounded words are words that do not accord with the Way of the Mean; if one listens to them, they will certainly do harm to governance. Such words you must not listen to. Unconsulted plans are plans that do not accord with the Way of the Mean; if one employs them, they too will certainly do harm to governance. Such plans you must not employ. If you act thus, the internal and the external will mutually support one another, and the Way of governance will be complete. Yet if one upholds it without reverence, how can one preserve that good governance? Therefore, the one who rules over the people is the sovereign—is the sovereign not worthy of love? Those who are governed by the sovereign are the people—are the people not worthy of awe? Why is this so? Because without their sovereign, even though the people number in the hundreds of millions, they have no one to revere and support; this is why the sovereign is worthy of love. And without his people, even though the sovereign possesses the impregnability of metal walls and boiling moats, he has no one with whom to defend the state; this is why the people are worthy of awe. Since sovereign and people depend on one another like this, now that you are about to act as sovereign and govern the people, how could you not be reverent? You must be cautious and fearful, being careful of your position as Son of Heaven, not allowing the laxity of a single thought or a single day to leave behind great sorrow or invite distant calamity; and you must tremble with vigilance and rouse yourself to cultivate the goodness that is desirable, not letting the slightest bit or a single instance of evil arise in your mind and do harm to your governance. If you do so, then the Way of being careful in your position will be fulfilled, and as sovereign you will possess the reality of being worthy of love—what reason would there still be to stand in awe of the people? The Way of achieving and preserving good governance indeed reaches its utmost here, and nothing can be added to it." Alas! The Mean is the method of the mind transmitted from sage to sage, and reverence is that whereby sage learning achieves both its beginning and its end. When a ruler governs the empire, without the Mean the foundation for achieving good governance is not established; without reverence…

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
致治之道或幾乎故帝舜有見乎此而舉以命之於
禹厥後有夏傳之以為家法此所以久安長治而
非後世所能及歟
凡厥庶民無有淫朋人無有比德惟皇作極凡
厥庶民有猷有為有守汝則念之不恊于極
不罹于咎皇則受之而康而色曰予攸好德
汝則錫之福時人斯其惟皇之極無虐煢獨
而畏高明人之有能有為使羞其行而邦其
昌凡厥正人既富方穀
同考試官學正方批此一題本難該括是篇能斂華就實醇
正典雅必究心於經學者
考試官教諭趙批題雖長而意實相承此作得之
考試官教授戴批理明詞暢表而出之
民臣從化而無惡由君有以儀刑之民臣感化有
淺深在君所當造就之盖君之建極實民臣所係
以觀化也然所感有淺深苟不委曲造就之何以
使之悉歸於極哉箕子衍皇極之疇為武王告其
punctuated:
致治之道或幾乎。故帝舜有見乎此，而舉以命之於禹。厥後有夏傳之以為家法，此所以久安長治，而非後世所能及歟！

凡厥庶民，無有淫朋；人無有比德，惟皇作極。凡厥庶民，有猷有為有守，汝則念之。不恊于極，不罹于咎，皇則受之。而康而色，曰：「予攸好德。」汝則錫之福，時人斯其惟皇之極。無虐煢獨，而畏高明。人之有能有為，使羞其行，而邦其昌。凡厥正人，既富方穀。
〔同考試官學正方批：此一題本難該括，是篇能斂華就實，醇正典雅，必究心於經學者。〕
〔考試官教諭趙批：題雖長而意實相承，此作得之。〕
〔考試官教授戴批：理明詞暢，表而出之。〕

民臣從化而無惡，由君有以儀刑之；民臣感化有淺深，在君所當造就之。盖君之建極，實民臣所係以觀化也。然所感有淺深，苟不委曲造就之，何以使之悉歸於極哉？箕子衍皇極之疇，為武王告，其…
translation_en:
… the way of bringing about order would almost cease [?]. Therefore, Emperor Shun perceived this and raised it in his charge to Yu. Thereafter, the House of Xia transmitted it as their family law; is this not why they enjoyed enduring peace and lasting order beyond what later ages could attain?

"Among all the common people, there shall be no licentious factions; among officials, there shall be no partisan collusions: it is the Sovereign who establishes the Supreme Standard. Among all the common people, when they have counsel, have activity, and have self-regulation, you should bear them in mind. Those who do not yet conform to the Supreme Standard and yet do not fall into crime, the Sovereign should receive them. When a placid expression is on your face and someone says, 'What I love is virtue,' you should confer blessings (official emoluments) upon him; that person will thus conform to the Sovereign's Supreme Standard. Do not oppress the helpless and solitary, while fearing the high and illustrious. When men have ability and activity, cause them to advance their conduct, and the state will prosper. All upright men, having been enriched, will then be good."
[Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Subprefectural Director of Studies: This passage as a topic is inherently difficult to encompass as a whole, yet this essay restrains floridness in favor of substance; pure, upright, classic, and refined, its author must be one who has devoted his mind to the study of the Classics.]
[Comment by Examiner Zhao, District Director of Studies: Although the topic passage is long, its ideas are in fact sequentially connected; this composition has grasped that.]
[Comment by Examiner Dai, Prefectural Director of Studies: The reasoning is clear and the diction fluent; we single it out for presentation.]

That the people and ministers follow transforming influence and are free of evil is because the ruler provides a model for them to imitate; that the people and ministers are moved by transforming influence to varying depths means that it rests with the ruler to cultivate and bring them to completion. For the ruler's establishment of the Supreme Standard is truly what the people and ministers depend upon in observing his transforming influence. Yet what they are moved by varies in depth; if he does not painstakingly cultivate and bring them to completion, how can he cause all of them to return to the Supreme Standard? When the Viscount of Ji (Jizi) elaborated the category of the Sovereign's Supreme Standard to instruct King Wu, his …

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
意如此請申之環居宇內者庶民也徧為爾德而
無邪黨之行是豈自能惟君為之極使之有所取
正焉布列庶位者人也各恭乃職而無比附之私
亦非自克惟皇之作極俾之有所視效耳夫下之
觀化有係於君如此君固不可不建極也然人之
生稟有不同感化不能無淺深君可不有以造就
之乎故凡民之有猷有為有守者其才有用其
德有可永君當念之而不忘不協于極不罹于咎
者進之可與為善棄之則流於惡君當受之而不
===
拒焉迨其見於外而有安和之色發於中而有好
德之言汝於是則錫之以福與之以祿而是人斯
其惟皇之極矣然成民之才當無間於至微雖煢
獨之有善亦當勸之而不忽成臣之才當無間於
至顯雖高明有不善亦當戒之而勿畏故凡人之
有才智者必使之進於善凡有設施者必勉之羞
其行則官使皆賢才而國可底于明昌矣然禮義
生於富足彼在官者必先富之以祿使俯仰皆足
繼之以廩俾好于而家然後驅而之善責其進行
punctuated: 意如此，請申之。環居宇內者，庶民也。徧為爾德，而無邪黨之行，是豈自能？惟君為之極，使之有所取正焉。布列庶位者，人也。各恭乃職，而無比附之私，亦非自克，惟皇之作極，俾之有所視效耳。夫下之觀化有係於君如此，君固不可不建極也。然人之生稟有不同，感化不能無淺深，君可不有以造就之乎？故凡民之有猷、有為、有守者，其才有用，其德有可永，君當念之而不忘；不協于極、不罹于咎者，進之可與為善，棄之則流於惡，君當受之而不拒焉。迨其見於外而有安和之色，發於中而有好德之言，汝於是則錫之以福，與之以祿，而是人斯其惟皇之極矣。然成民之才，當無間於至微，雖煢獨之有善，亦當勸之而不忽；成臣之才，當無間於至顯，雖高明有不善，亦當戒之而勿畏。故凡人之有才智者，必使之進於善；凡有設施者，必勉之羞其行，則官使皆賢才，而國可底于明昌矣。然禮義生於富足，彼在官者，必先富之以祿，使俯仰皆足，繼之以廩，俾好于而家，然後驅而之善，責其進行，
translation_en: … meaning is like this; allow me to elaborate upon it. Those who dwell throughout the realm are the common people. That they universally practice your virtue without engaging in perverse factionalism—how could they be capable of this on their own? It is only because the ruler serves as the standard for them, giving them something by which to rectify themselves. Those who are arrayed in the various offices are the officials. That each respectfully attends to his duties without the selfishness of partisan collusion is likewise not achieved by their own self-mastery; it is only because the sovereign establishes the standard, giving them something to observe and emulate. Now, since the transformation of those below by observing their superiors depends upon the ruler to such a degree, the ruler certainly cannot fail to establish the supreme standard. Yet because people differ in their innate endowments, the depth to which they are moved and transformed cannot be uniform; how can the ruler fail to have means to cultivate and bring them to completion? Therefore, among all the common people, those who have計画 (counsels), who have action, and who have self-restraint possess talents that are useful and virtues that can endure; the ruler ought to keep them in mind and not forget them. As for those who do not yet conform to the supreme standard and yet have not fallen into transgression—if advanced, they can be led to do good, whereas if abandoned, they will slide into evil; the ruler ought to receive them and not reject them. When it shows in their outward demeanor as a calm and harmonious countenance, and issues from within as words declaring: "What I love is virtue," then you should bestow blessings upon them and grant them emoluments, and thus these persons will also conform to the sovereign's supreme standard. Yet in bringing the talents of the people to completion, there should be no neglect of the most humble: even if the solitary and friendless possess goodness, one ought to encourage them and not overlook them. And in bringing the talents of officials to completion, there should be no exception for the most illustrious: even if the high and eminent have faults, one ought to admonish them and not stand in awe of them. Thus, all men in office who possess talent and wisdom must be caused to advance in goodness, and all who undertake administrative measures must be urged to advance their conduct; then those employed in office will all be worthy talents, and the state can attain brightness and prosperity. Nevertheless, propriety and righteousness arise from sufficiency. For those in office, one must first enrich them with emoluments so that they have enough to support both superiors and dependents, and continue to supply them from the granaries so that things go well in their households; only after that, if one drives them toward goodness and demands that they advance in conduct, …

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
殆有所顧藉而惟日其邁矣夫隨才造就曲成不
遺如此則民人豈復有淫朋比德者哉由是而觀
皇極不建固無以率人化造就無方又何以成人
才建極使下觀而化者立教之本也造就使激勵
而進者陶成之術也不惟立極以化之而又造就
以成之此皇極所以無棄人也箕子為武王陳洪
範而獨詳於皇極者如此豈特武王之所當知實
天下萬世人主之龜鑑歟
詩
===
稱彼兕觥萬壽無疆
吳珎
同考試官訓導孫批此篇形容邠民忠愛其君之至宛然
在目讀之令人興起宜寘高選
同考試官訓導王批題本平易佳者最少惟此篇可觀
同考試官訓導吳批邠民之相戒也禮雖野而意甚真周
家世三十年八百基於此歟
考試官教諭趙批邠俗之厚此作得之
考試官教授戴批邠民忠愛之意周家風化之厚
punctuated:
殆有所顧藉，而惟日其邁矣。夫隨才造就、曲成不遺如此，則民人豈復有淫朋比德者哉？由是而觀，皇極不建，固無以率人化；造就無方，又何以成人才？建極使下觀而化者，立教之本也；造就使激勵而進者，陶成之術也。不惟立極以化之，而又造就以成之，此皇極所以無棄人也。箕子為武王陳《洪範》而獨詳於皇極者如此，豈特武王之所當知，實天下萬世人主之龜鑑歟！
詩
稱彼兕觥，萬壽無疆。
吳珎
〔同考試官訓導孫批：此篇形容邠民忠愛其君之至，宛然在目，讀之令人興起，宜寘高選。〕
〔同考試官訓導王批：題本平易，佳者最少，惟此篇可觀。〕
〔同考試官訓導吳批：邠民之相戒也，禮雖野而意甚真，周家世三十、年八百基於此歟？〕
〔考試官教諭趙批：邠俗之厚，此作得之。〕
〔考試官教授戴批：邠民忠愛之意，周家風化之厚，
translation_en:
…they will surely have something to cherish and rely upon, and thus strive forward day by day. Now, when men are cultivated according to their talents and brought to fulfillment in every particular without anyone being left behind like this, how could there still be any among the common people who form licentious factions or collude in vice? Viewed from this perspective, if the Supreme Ultimate is not established, there is indeed no means to lead people to transformation; yet if cultivation lacks a proper method, how can men of talent be brought to completion? Establishing the standard so that those below behold it and are transformed is the foundation of instituting moral instruction; cultivating them so that they are roused and encouraged to advance is the art of molding and perfecting them. Not only establishing the standard to transform them, but also cultivating them to bring them to completion—this is why under the Supreme Ultimate no man is cast aside. That Jizi, in setting forth the "Great Plan" (Hongfan) for King Wu, was so uniquely detailed regarding the Supreme Ultimate—is this merely what King Wu ought to have known? Truly, it is a mirror and exemplar for rulers of all under Heaven for ten thousand generations!

Classic of Poetry (Shi)
"They raise the rhinoceros-horn cup: 'Myriad years of life without bound!'"
Wu Zhen
[Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor: This essay depicts to perfection the utmost loyalty and affection of the people of Bin for their ruler, making it vivid before one's eyes. Reading it inspires one to rise up; it ought to be placed in a high rank.]
[Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: The topic is inherently plain and easy, yet fine essays on it are very few; only this piece is worthy of note.]
[Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor: In the mutual exhortations of the people of Bin, though their rites are rustic, their sentiments are most genuine. Was not the Zhou house's endurance for thirty generations and eight hundred years founded upon this?]
[Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: Thegenerous customs of Bin are captured by this composition.]
[Comment by Examiner Dai, Professor: The loyal and affectionate sentiments of the people of Bin and the richness of the transformative customs of the Zhou house…]

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於斯乎見矣
欲舉酒而祝君壽此豳民之忠愛也蓋人君之福
莫大乎壽也今豳民相戒舉酒而祝君壽此所以
為忠愛之至也歟念昔豳民當農事既畢之時相
戒滌塲之際意蓋曰衣我食我享公之賜厚矣豈
可忘所自乎彼其我朱孔陽為公子裳固嘗少效
慇懃而忠上之誠未已也我將舉兕觥之酒於公
堂雖以賤瀆貴而不顧焉取彼狐狸為公子裘固
嘗少伸勤渠而愛君之私未罄也我將舉兕觥之
===
酒於公所雖以卑瀆尊而不計焉然所以舉酒於
君惟欲祝其壽耳蓋吾君富有豳矣富而非壽何
以長守富耶但願萬壽無疆長守其富而為吾民
之父母也吾君貴為公矣貴而非壽何以長守貴
耶但願萬壽無期長守其貴而為吾民之主宰也
吁豳民舉酒而祝壽於君禮雖野而意則真物雖
薄而情則厚謂非忠愛之至可乎抑考是詩周公
以成王未知稼穡之艱難故陳后稷公劉風化之
所由以教之一詩之中汲汲乎衣食之始終拳拳
punctuated:
於斯乎見矣。
欲舉酒而祝君壽，此豳民之忠愛也。蓋人君之福，莫大乎壽也。今豳民相戒，舉酒而祝君壽，此所以為忠愛之至也歟！念昔豳民當農事既畢之時，相戒滌塲之際，意蓋曰：衣我食我，享公之賜厚矣，豈可忘所自乎？彼其「我朱孔陽，為公子裳」，固嘗少效慇懃，而忠上之誠未已也；我將舉兕觥之酒於公堂，雖以賤瀆貴而不顧焉。「取彼狐狸，為公子裘」，固嘗少伸勤渠，而愛君之私未罄也；我將舉兕觥之酒於公所，雖以卑瀆尊而不計焉。然所以舉酒於君，惟欲祝其壽耳。蓋吾君富有豳矣，富而非壽，何以長守富耶？但願萬壽無疆，長守其富，而為吾民之父母也。吾君貴為公矣，貴而非壽，何以長守貴耶？但願萬壽無期，長守其貴，而為吾民之主宰也。吁！豳民舉酒而祝壽於君，禮雖野而意則真，物雖薄而情則厚，謂非忠愛之至可乎？抑考是詩，周公以成王未知稼穡之艱難，故陳后稷、公劉風化之所由以教之。一詩之中，汲汲乎衣食之始終，拳拳
translation_en:
…are seen right here.
Wishing to raise wine and pray for their ruler's longevity—this is the loyal affection of the people of Bin. Indeed, among the blessings of a ruler, none is greater than longevity. Now the people of Bin exhort one another to raise wine and pray for their ruler's longevity; is this not the ultimate expression of loyal affection? Recalling the people of Bin of old, when the agricultural work was finished and they exhorted one another at the time of sweeping the threshing floors, their thought was surely thus: "Clothing us and feeding us, we have enjoyed the generous bounty of our Duke; how could we forget whence it comes? As for 'our red dye so bright, to make lower garments for the Duke's sons,' we have indeed offered a small token of earnest devotion, yet our sincere loyalty to our superior is not exhausted; we shall raise the wine in the rhinoceros-horn goblet in the Duke's hall, not hesitating even though we, being lowly, intrude upon the noble. As for 'taking those foxes and wildcats, to make furs for the Duke's sons,' we have indeed slightly expressed our diligent care, yet our personal affection for our ruler is not fully spent; we shall raise the wine in the rhinoceros-horn goblet at the Duke's residence, not reckoning even though we, being humble, presume upon the exalted." Yet the reason they raise wine to their ruler is solely that they wish to pray for his longevity. For our ruler possesses the wealth of Bin; if he is wealthy but does not have long life, how can he long preserve his wealth? We only wish him myriad years of boundless life, so that he may long preserve his wealth and be the father and mother of us, the people. Our ruler holds the noble rank of Duke; if he is noble but does not have long life, how can he long preserve his nobility? We only wish him myriad years of endless life, so that he may long preserve his nobility and be the master of us, the people. Ah! When the people of Bin raise wine to pray for their ruler's longevity, although the ritual is rustic, their intention is genuine; although the offering is slight, their feeling is deep. How could one say this is not the ultimate expression of loyal affection? Moreover, examining this ode, because King Cheng did not yet know the hardships of sowing and reaping, the Duke of Zhou set forth the origins of the moral transformation wrought by Hou Ji and Duke Liu in order to instruct him. Throughout the single ode, there is unceasing attention to the beginning and end of providing clothing and food, and earnest devotion…

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
乎上下之忠愛厥後成王果知務農重穀為有周
守成之令主而享鳧鷖既醉之太平得非周公告
戒之力歟
皇皇者華于彼原隰駪駪征夫每懷靡及我馬
維駒六轡如濡載馳載驅周爰咨諏我馬維
騏六轡如絲載馳載驅周爰咨謀我馬維駱
六轡沃若載馳載驅周爰咨度我馬維駟六
轡既均載馳載驅周爰咨詢
童潮
===
同考試官訓導孫批此題本長作者多泛冗不切
惟此篇詳明簡當一結尤出人
意表非老於葩經者殆不能也宜
寘前列
同考試官訓導王批此題不難於豐而難於簡
簡而明可取也
同考試官訓導吳批詞婉順而意和平深得先王
教戒使臣之旨
考試官教諭趙批此篇融註成文得遣使臣之旨
punctuated:
乎上下之忠愛。厥後成王果知務農重穀，為有周守成之令主，而享《鳧鷖》、《既醉》之太平，得非周公告戒之力歟？

「皇皇者華，于彼原隰。駪駪征夫，每懷靡及。我馬維駒，六轡如濡。載馳載驅，周爰咨諏。我馬維騏，六轡如絲。載馳載驅，周爰咨謀。我馬維駱，六轡沃若。載馳載驅，周爰咨度。我馬維駟，六轡既均。載馳載驅，周爰咨詢。」
童潮
同考試官訓導孫批：此題本長，作者多泛冗不切，惟此篇詳明簡當，一結尤出人意表，非老於《葩經》者殆不能也，宜寘前列。
同考試官訓導王批：此題不難於豐而難於簡，簡而明，可取也。
同考試官訓導吳批：詞婉順而意和平，深得先王教戒使臣之旨。
考試官教諭趙批：此篇融註成文，得遣使臣之旨。
translation_en:
… devoted to the loyalty and affection between ruler and ruled. Thereafter, King Cheng indeed understood the importance of attending to agriculture and valuing grain, becoming an admirable ruler who preserved the achievements of the Zhou house and enjoying the grand peace celebrated in the odes "Wild Ducks and Widgeons" (Fu yi) and "Already Drunk with Wine" (Ji zui). Was this not due to the power of the Duke of Zhou's admonitions?

"Brilliant are the flowers, on those plains and lowlands. / Numerous are the traveling men, each fearing he will fall short. / My horses are colts, the six reins seem moistened. / I gallop and I drive, everywhere inquiring and taking counsel. / My horses are dappled grays, the six reins are like silk. / I gallop and I drive, everywhere inquiring and planning. / My horses are white with black manes, the six reins are glossy. / I gallop and I drive, everywhere inquiring and deliberating. / My horses are iron-grays, the six reins are well-balanced. / I gallop and I drive, everywhere inquiring and consulting."
Tong Chao 童潮
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Sun comments: This topic is inherently long, and most writers become diffuse, wordy, and off the mark. Only this essay is detailed, clear, concise, and apt. Its conclusion in particular surpasses all expectations; someone not thoroughly versed in the Classic of Poetry (Pajing) would scarcely be capable of it. It ought to be placed in the front ranks.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wang comments: With this topic, what is difficult is not abundance, but conciseness. Concise yet clear, it is worthy of selection.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wu comments: The diction is graceful and smooth, and the meaning harmonious and balanced. It deeply grasps the purport of the former kings in instructing and admonishing their envoys.
Examiner and Instructor Zhao comments: This essay blends the commentary seamlessly into the prose, capturing the purport of dispatching envoys.

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授戴批述其所懷而勉其職非此作
其孰能形容之乎
王者之遣使臣既托興行道之勤而恐不能盡其
職必歷叙行道之勤而求所以盡其職盖使臣貴
乎盡其職也今既恐其有所不盡得不求所以盡
之哉王者遣使之際托興於前而歷言於後其亦
因以教戒也歟昔周王之遣使臣美其行道之勤
而述其心之所懷曰彼皇皇然而鮮明者草木之
華也則生于高平之原下濕之隰矣此駪駪然而
===
衆多疾行者使臣與其属也則恐上德不能宣下
情不能達而常若有所不及矣使臣每懷靡及如
此抑将何所務哉彼駕車之四牡則維駒也御駒
之六轡則如濡也于以載馳載驅而周於咨諏以
補其不及焉駕車之四馬則維騏也制騏之六轡
則如絲也于以載馳載驅而周於咨謀以補其不
及焉以至駕彼四駱而六轡則沃若也馳驅不已
而咨度之必周也度焉而周非所以補其不及乎
乘其四駰而六轡則既均也馳驅不已而咨詢之
punctuated:
考試官教授戴批：述其所懷而勉其職，非此作其孰能形容之乎？
王者之遣使臣，既托興行道之勤，而恐不能盡其職，必歷叙行道之勤，而求所以盡其職。盖使臣貴乎盡其職也，今既恐其有所不盡，得不求所以盡之哉？王者遣使之際，托興於前而歷言於後，其亦因以教戒也歟！昔周王之遣使臣，美其行道之勤，而述其心之所懷曰：彼皇皇然而鮮明者，草木之華也，則生于高平之原、下濕之隰矣；此駪駪然而衆多疾行者，使臣與其属也，則恐上德不能宣、下情不能達，而常若有所不及矣。使臣每懷靡及如此，抑将何所務哉？彼駕車之四牡，則維駒也；御駒之六轡，則如濡也。于以載馳載驅，而周於咨諏，以補其不及焉。駕車之四馬，則維騏也；制騏之六轡，則如絲也。于以載馳載驅，而周於咨謀，以補其不及焉。以至駕彼四駱，而六轡則沃若也，馳驅不已，而咨度之必周也；度焉而周，非所以補其不及乎？乘其四駰，而六轡則既均也，馳驅不已，而咨詢之
translation_en:
Examiner and Confucian Instructor Dai comments: Recounting what they cherish in their hearts and exhorting them to fulfill their duties—if not for this composition, who could have depicted it so well?

When the true king dispatches his envoys, having first used an evocative metaphor to praise their diligence on the road and their fear of failing to fulfill their duties, he must then recount in detail their diligence on the road and their search for the means to fulfill those duties. For what is valued in an envoy is the fulfillment of his duty; since he already fears falling short in some respect, how could he not seek the means to fulfill it completely? When the king dispatches his envoys, using an evocative metaphor at the outset and speaking at length thereafter, is it not also his way of instructing and admonishing them?

In antiquity, when the King of Zhou dispatched his envoys, he praised their diligence on the road and recounted what they cherished in their hearts, saying: Those things that are so brilliant and fresh are the blossoms of plants and trees, growing upon the high, level plains and in the low, damp marshes. Those who travel so numerously and swiftly are the envoy and his retinue, fearing lest the ruler's virtue fail to be proclaimed above and the people's conditions fail to be communicated from below, constantly feeling as though they might fall short. Since the envoy ever cherishes this anxiety of falling short, to what then shall he devote his efforts? Those four stallions drawing his carriage are young colts, and the six reins controlling the colts are as if moistened and glossy; thus he gallops and drives on, making thorough inquiries into affairs of state to make up for where he falls short. The four horses drawing his carriage are dappled grays, and the six reins controlling the dappled grays are like fine silk; thus he gallops and drives on, taking thorough counsel to make up for where he falls short. Furthermore, he yokes those four white-maned black horses, with the six reins so supple and sleek, galloping and driving without cease to deliberate thoroughly on what is proper—and in deliberating so thoroughly, is this not how he makes up for where he falls short? He mounts his carriage drawn by four铁-gray and white-speckled horses, with the six reins well-balanced and even, galloping and driving without cease to question…

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
□□□□詢焉而猶又非所以補其不及乎若然則
上德宣而下情達矣使臣之職庸有不盡者乎吁
王者之遣使也教戒之辭藹然溢於詠歌之表忠
厚之意一何至哉抑又考之此詩所以遣使臣而
四牡所以勞使臣也先王之於使臣一遣一勞而
必重之以詩抑何恩禮之至歟盖君非使臣而德
無以宣之民民非使臣而情無以達之君使乎使
乎其有補於治道矣乎於乎古之王者聽徹閭閻
而明見萬里有由然夫
===
春秋
鄭人來輸平〔隱公六年〕宋人及楚人平〔宣公十五年〕
王岐
同考試官學正孟批二傳道義功利之說𫝊盡魯鄭
宋楚結平之意是篇得旨行文老健宜居首選
考試官教諭趙批發明正誼明道之旨允合傳意
考試官教授熊批得聖人謹嚴之法故錄之
釋怨出於私者春秋著其罪解釁由於下者春秋
惡其專此見魯鄭宋楚之平皆非聖人之所予也
punctuated:
□□□□；詢焉而猶，又非所以補其不及乎？若然，則上德宣而下情達矣，使臣之職庸有不盡者乎？吁！王者之遣使也，教戒之辭藹然溢於詠歌之表，忠厚之意一何至哉！抑又考之，此詩所以遣使臣，而《四牡》所以勞使臣也。先王之於使臣，一遣一勞，而必重之以詩，抑何恩禮之至歟！盖君非使臣，而德無以宣之民；民非使臣，而情無以達之君。使乎！使乎！其有補於治道矣乎！於乎！古之王者，聽徹閭閻而明見萬里，有由然夫！
春秋
鄭人來輸平〔隱公六年〕、宋人及楚人平〔宣公十五年〕
王岐
同考試官學正孟批：二傳道義功利之說，𫝊盡魯鄭、宋楚結平之意。是篇得旨，行文老健，宜居首選。
考試官教諭趙批：發明正誼明道之旨，允合傳意。
考試官教授熊批：得聖人謹嚴之法，故錄之。
釋怨出於私者，《春秋》著其罪；解釁由於下者，《春秋》惡其專。此見魯、鄭、宋、楚之平，皆非聖人之所予也。
translation_en:
… [four characters illegible]; by inquiring and planning, is this not also how he makes up for what he feels he has failed to reach? If it is so, then the ruler's virtue is proclaimed above and the conditions of the people below are communicated; how could the duties of an envoy fail to be fully discharged? Ah! When the true king dispatches an envoy, his words of instruction and admonition overflow warmly beyond the surface of song and verse—how supreme is his loyal and generous intent! Moreover, if we examine it further, this ode was used to send off envoys, whereas the ode "Four Steeds" (Si mu) was used to reward their toil. In dealing with their envoys, the former kings, whether sending them off or rewarding their toil, invariably honored the occasion with an ode—how utmost were their grace and courtesy! For without envoys, the ruler has no means to proclaim his virtue to the people, and without envoys, the people have no means to communicate their conditions to the ruler. Envoys, oh envoys! How greatly do they contribute to the way of governance! Alas, that the kings of antiquity could hear all the way to the humblest village lanes and see clearly for ten thousand li—there was truly a reason for this!

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"The men of Zheng came to offer peace" [6th year of Duke Yin]; "The men of Song and the men of Chu made peace" [15th year of Duke Xuan].

Wang Qi 王岐

Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Meng comments: The discussions of moral principle versus utilitarian profit in the two commentaries exhaustively convey the meaning of the peace agreements concluded between Lu and Zheng, and between Song and Chu. This essay grasps the essential purport, and its style is mature and vigorous; it deserves to be placed at the head of those selected.

Examiner and County Instructor (jiaoyu) Zhao comments: It elucidates the principle of rectifying righteousness and clarifying the Way, truly conforming to the meaning of the commentary.

Examiner and Prefectural Instructor (jiaoshou) Xiong comments: It captures the Sage's strict and cautious method, and therefore we record it for publication.

When the relinquishing of grievances arises from selfish motives, the Spring and Autumn Annals exposes the guilt; when the resolving of hostilities originates from subordinates below, the Spring and Autumn Annals abhors their usurpation of authority. From this we see that the peace agreements between Lu and Zheng, and between Song and Chu, were in neither case approved by the Sage. …

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
嗟夫入春秋之始干戈敵仇盟誓固黨列國之人
心已虎狼相視矣於怨也相尋無已曾何釋之有
哉彼其懿親之鄭當我隱踐祚之先而有狐壤之
戰隱也見止鄭也克捷兩君之仇積不相下亦久
矣今也鄭莊知魯與宋有可乘之隙將結魯以行
夫報復之謀故一旦屈損求成以篤夫姻隣之舊
魯亦溺夫賄賂之交今日歸祊明日取邑抑斯意
也豈誠欲以心而相敬哉豈誠欲以義而相睦哉
亦豈誠欲彼此釋舊憾而為玉帛之好哉不過合
===
黨自私以成貪利之計爾噫問其名則是究其實
則非奚取乎聖人以大公至正之道望於人於魯
鄭也何誅傳曰正其誼不謀其利盖如此及春秋
之中殺人盈城暴骨連莽諸侯之國勢已犬羊相
制矣於釁也相傾無間曾何解之有哉彼其貪婪
之楚因宋公申舟之戮而決蒲胥之師宋也被圍
楚也肆虐兩國之民厄於塗炭亦慘矣今也華元
畫内外講好之策與子反成交驩之謀故一夕潜
入楚師輕見其情實之危反亦語之以匱糧之急
punctuated:
嗟夫！入春秋之始，干戈敵仇，盟誓固黨，列國之人心已虎狼相視矣。於怨也，相尋無已，曾何釋之有哉？彼其懿親之鄭，當我隱踐祚之先，而有狐壤之戰。隱也見止，鄭也克捷，兩君之仇，積不相下亦久矣。今也鄭莊知魯與宋有可乘之隙，將結魯以行夫報復之謀，故一旦屈損求成，以篤夫姻隣之舊；魯亦溺夫賄賂之交，今日歸祊，明日取邑。抑斯意也，豈誠欲以心而相敬哉？豈誠欲以義而相睦哉？亦豈誠欲彼此釋舊憾而為玉帛之好哉？不過合黨自私，以成貪利之計爾。噫！問其名則是，究其實則非，奚取乎？聖人以大公至正之道望於人，於魯、鄭也何誅！傳曰「正其誼不謀其利」，盖如此。
及春秋之中，殺人盈城，暴骨連莽，諸侯之國勢已犬羊相制矣。於釁也，相傾無間，曾何解之有哉？彼其貪婪之楚，因宋公申舟之戮，而決蒲胥之師。宋也被圍，楚也肆虐，兩國之民，厄於塗炭亦慘矣。今也華元畫内外講好之策，與子反成交驩之謀，故一夕潜入楚師，輕見其情實之危；反亦語之以匱糧之急，
translation_en:
Alas! At the very beginning of the Spring and Autumn period, states warred as bitter enemies with shields and spears and consolidated factions through covenants and oaths; the minds of people across the various states already eyed one another like tigers and wolves. In their resentments, they pursued vengeance without end—how was there ever any letting go? Take Zheng, a state of close royal kinship: before our Duke Yin (Yin Gong) ascended the throne, there took place the battle of Hurang. Duke Yin was captured and detained, while Zheng won the victory; the enmity between the two rulers had accumulated without either yielding for a long time. Now Duke Zhuang of Zheng (Zheng Zhuang), knowing that there was a rift between Lu and Song that could be exploited and intending to ally with Lu in order to carry out his plot of retaliation, suddenly humbled himself to sue for peace, ostensibly to renew the old ties of marriage and neighborly friendship. Lu, too, indulged in a relationship built on bribery—receiving the return of Beng today, seizing territories tomorrow. Yet in such intentions, did they truly wish to respect each other from the heart? Did they truly wish to live in harmony through righteousness? Or did they truly wish for both sides to let go of old grudges and forge a friendship of jade and silk? It was nothing more than banding together in selfish faction to accomplish a scheme of greedy profit. Alas! If one asks after the name, it seems right; if one examines the reality, it is wrong—what is there to approve in it? The Sage looked to men with the Way of supreme impartiality and utmost rectitude; how could he spare Lu and Zheng from condemnation! When the commentary says, "Rectify the principle and do not scheme for its profit," this is what it means.

By the middle of the Spring and Autumn period, the slain filled the cities and exposed bones stretched across the wilds; the power relations among the feudal lords already controlled one another like dogs and sheep. In their feuds, they subverted one another without pause—how was there ever any resolution? Take rapacious Chu: because the Duke of Song (Song Gong) executed Shen Zhou, Chu launched its army from the Puxu market. Song was besieged, Chu wreaked havoc, and the people of both states suffered miserably in mire and charcoal. Now Hua Yuan devised a stratagem for negotiating peace between the inside and outside, and formed a plan of mutual cordiality with Zifan. Thus in a single night he slipped into the Chu camp and lightly revealed the true peril of Song's situation; Zifan, in turn, told him of the urgency of Chu's shortage of grain, …

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
我無爾詐爾無我虞抑斯意也豈真能紓亡國之
憂乎豈真能避滅國之罪哉亦豈真能彼此賤欺
詐而惡侵伐之患哉蓋欲專權自恣以收平國之
功爾噫迹其事則順原其情則𠂻奚可乎聖人以
大公至正之道求於人於元反也何誅傳曰明其
道不計其功又如此吁責魯鄭者所以戒人之趨
利責宋楚者所以戒人之幸功聖人曷嘗容心於
其間哉因其人之罪而示夫斧鉞之嚴也區區功
利苟不以道義裁之則人之馳騖於挾私妄作者
===
天下皆是也雖然春秋謹嚴之法奚翅如斯而已
乎他如郜鼎之取衛俘之歸楚丘之城城濮之戰
皆原情定罪不少假借蓋與此意互相發讀經者
考之
晉人敗狄于交剛〔成公十二年〕公如京師遂會晉侯齊
侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯邾人滕人伐秦〔成公十三年〕
叔孫僑如會晉士燮齊高無咎宋華元衛孫
林父鄭公子鰌邾人會吳于鍾離〔成公十五年〕晉侯
及楚子鄭伯戰于鄢陵楚子鄭師敗績〔成公十六年〕
punctuated:
「我無爾詐，爾無我虞。」抑斯意也，豈真能紓亡國之憂乎？豈真能避滅國之罪哉？亦豈真能彼此賤欺詐而惡侵伐之患哉？蓋欲專權自恣，以收平國之功爾。噫！迹其事則順，原其情則𠂻，奚可乎？聖人以大公至正之道求於人，於元、反也何誅？《傳》曰：「明其道不計其功。」又如此。吁！責魯、鄭者，所以戒人之趨利；責宋、楚者，所以戒人之幸功。聖人曷嘗容心於其間哉？因其人之罪，而示夫斧鉞之嚴也。區區功利，苟不以道義裁之，則人之馳騖於挾私妄作者，天下皆是也。雖然，《春秋》謹嚴之法，奚翅如斯而已乎？他如郜鼎之取、衛俘之歸、楚丘之城、城濮之戰，皆原情定罪，不少假借，蓋與此意互相發，讀經者考之。

晉人敗狄于交剛〔成公十二年〕。公如京師，遂會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人、滕人伐秦〔成公十三年〕。叔孫僑如會晉士燮、齊高無咎、宋華元、衛孫林父、鄭公子鰌、邾人會吳于鍾離〔成公十五年〕。晉侯及楚子、鄭伯戰于鄢陵，楚子、鄭師敗績〔成公十六年〕。…
translation_en:
… “I shall not deceive you, and do not you suspect me.” Yet as for this intention, could it truly relieve the anxiety of a perishing state? Could it truly avoid the crime of destroying a state? Or could it truly cause both sides to despise deceit and abhor the calamity of invasion and attack? In truth, they merely wished to monopolize power and act willfully in order to claim the merit of pacifying their states! Alas! If one traces their deeds, they appear compliant; if one examines their motives, they are crooked [𠂻, for 邪]. How could that be acceptable? The Sage demands of men the Way of utmost impartiality and supreme rectitude; in the case of Hua Yuan and Zifan, what condemnation was spared? When the commentary says, “Clarify the Way without calculating its merit,” it refers to just such a case.

Ah! Reproaching Lu and Zheng was the means to warn men against pursuing profit; reproaching Song and Chu was the means to warn men against coveting merit. How did the Sage ever harbor personal bias in the matter? On the basis of those men’s crimes, he displayed the severity of the battle-axe. Petty merit and profit—if they are not regulated by morality and righteousness, then people galloping after selfish schemes and reckless actions will fill the entire world. Even so, is the strict and rigorous method of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) limited merely to this? Other cases—such as the seizing of the tripod of Gao, the presentation of the captives from Wei, the walling of Chuqiu, and the Battle of Chengpu—all determine guilt by examining the underlying motives, without the slightest leniency. Indeed, they mutually illuminate this very meaning; let readers of the Classic examine them.

The men of Jin defeated the Di at Jiaogang [twelfth year of Duke Cheng]. The Duke went to the Capital, and thereupon joined the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, a man of Zhu, and a man of Teng in invading Qin [thirteenth year of Duke Cheng]. Shusun Qiaoru met with Shi Xie of Jin, Gao Wujiu of Qi, Hua Yuan of Song, Sun Linfu of Wei, Gongzi Qiu of Zheng, and a man of Zhu to meet Wu at Zhongli [fifteenth year of Duke Cheng]. The Marquis of Jin fought with the Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng at Yanling; the Viscount of Chu and the army of Zheng suffered a crushing defeat [sixteenth year of Duke Cheng]. …

見公晉人執季孫行父舍之于苕丘〔成公十六年〕公
會尹子單子晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯曹伯邾人

考試官教諭趙批題目本難作者多失旨是篇斷制
===
明白宜在所取
考試官教授戴批褒貶停當行文典實宜列高選
春秋幸霸功之迭著而惜霸德之屢隳于以見晉
厲之行事無服人心之道也慨自文襄遞往成景
荐衰世霸之烈已旁落于一時敵國之情常睥睨
乎四境霸中夏者苟不先剪其所忌奚可乎厲公
嗣業計幸出此以為秦狄合黨連兵來伐蓋嘗撓
我制楚之謀也此不治則無以立其威故首出偏

punctuated:
公會晉侯、齊侯、衛侯、宋華元、邾人于沙隨，不見公。晉人執季孫行父，舍之于苕丘。〔成公十六年〕公會尹子、單子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、邾人伐鄭。〔成公十七年〕同盟于柯陵。公會單子、晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊人、邾人伐鄭。〔同上〕
姚旿
同考試官學正盧批：此題諸作，議論紛紛，分截不明。惟此篇寫出晉厲行事得失，脗合傳意，故表而出之。
考試官教諭趙批：題目本難，作者多失旨。是篇斷制明白，宜在所取。
考試官教授戴批：褒貶停當，行文典實，宜列高選。
《春秋》幸霸功之迭著，而惜霸德之屢隳，于以見晉厲之行事無服人心之道也。慨自文、襄遞往，成、景荐衰，世霸之烈已旁落于一時，敵國之情常睥睨乎四境。霸中夏者，苟不先剪其所忌，奚可乎？厲公嗣業，計幸出此，以為秦、狄合黨連兵來伐，蓋嘗撓我制楚之謀也。此不治，則無以立其威，故首出偏師以破狄，而敗于交剛；繼會京師以挫秦，而戰于
translation_en:
The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Marquis of Wei, Hua Yuan of Song, and representatives of Zhu at Shasui, but was not received in audience. The men of Jin seized Jisun Xingfu and confined him at Tiaoqiu. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Cheng〕 The Duke joined Viscount Yin, Viscount Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and representatives of Zhu in attacking Zheng. 〔Seventeenth year of Duke Cheng〕 They entered into a joint covenant at Keling. The Duke joined Viscount Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and representatives of Qi and Zhu in attacking Zheng. 〔Same as above〕
Yao Wu 姚旿
Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, School Instructor: The essays on this topic offer a welter of arguments without clearly distinguishing their parts. This essay alone sets out the successes and failures of Duke Li of Jin’s actions in accord with the meaning of the commentary. I have therefore singled it out for presentation.
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: The topic is inherently difficult, and most writers miss its purport. This essay makes clear judgments and deserves selection.
Comment by Examiner Dai, Professor: Its praise and blame are appropriate, and its writing is classically grounded and substantial. It deserves a high place among the selected essays.
The Spring and Autumn Annals welcomes the successive achievements of hegemonic power but regrets the repeated collapse of hegemonic virtue. This reveals that Duke Li of Jin’s conduct lacked the means to win people’s hearts. Alas, after Dukes Wen and Xiang had passed away in succession, and decline had continued under Dukes Cheng and Jing, the glorious achievements of their hereditary hegemony had already slipped from their grasp. Rival states constantly eyed their borders covetously. How could anyone exercise hegemony over the central states without first cutting down the powers he feared? When Duke Li inherited this undertaking, his plans fortunately followed this course. He considered that Qin and the Di had formed an alliance and joined forces to invade, thereby previously disrupting Jin’s plans to restrain Chu. Unless this was dealt with, he could not establish his authority. Thus he first dispatched a detached force to crush the Di and defeated them at Jiaogang; next he joined the assembly at the royal capital to check Qin and fought at …

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
□隧狄服而秦恐則西北之憂弭矣吳楚構兵流
毒諸姬蓋將分我主霸之權也此不圖則無以舉
其職遂大合邦君通吳于鍾離而約束來同再蒐
卒乘捷楚于鄢陵而夷氛殄滅吳成而楚弱則東
南之慮消矣風聲駿歷於後先威畧振蕩乎中外
四強退聽外警少寧晉之霸功次第大槩有可觀
矣是時也慎乃脩履圖惟厥終以懷來者尚庶幾
哉厲也志不在大汰心易生如人望者魯列辟所
瞻當親之也苟拒之則無以屬人心故沙隨之會
===
乃入僑如之諧不見我公以絶其好苕丘之執爰
聽郤犫之請求多季孫以快其欲君辱而臣執則
我魯之心二矣携貳者鄭盛衰所係當懷之也苟
虐之則無以勸諸侯始焉致討率列國以臨戎而
尹單啓行繼焉往伐盟柯陵以出師而王臣再屈
上瀆而下凌則貳國之心叛矣遠近由是而解體
奸雄以之而窺伺舉動一失大勢已去晉之霸德
至此掃地而無遺矣春秋所以幸其功之著而惜
其德之隳者有由然也吁輕逞輙快者無大畧堅
punctuated: □隧，狄服而秦恐，則西北之憂弭矣。吳、楚構兵，流毒諸姬，蓋將分我主霸之權也。此不圖，則無以舉其職。遂大合邦君，通吳于鍾離，而約束來同；再蒐卒乘，捷楚于鄢陵，而夷氛殄滅。吳成而楚弱，則東南之慮消矣。風聲駿歷於後先，威畧振蕩乎中外。四強退聽，外警少寧，晉之霸功次第，大槩有可觀矣。是時也，慎乃脩履，圖惟厥終，以懷來者，尚庶幾哉！厲也志不在大，汰心易生。如人望者魯，列辟所瞻，當親之也。苟拒之，則無以屬人心。故沙隨之會，乃入僑如之諧，不見我公，以絶其好；苕丘之執，爰聽郤犫之請，求多季孫，以快其欲。君辱而臣執，則我魯之心二矣。携貳者鄭，盛衰所係，當懷之也。苟虐之，則無以勸諸侯。始焉致討，率列國以臨戎，而尹、單啓行；繼焉往伐，盟柯陵以出師，而王臣再屈。上瀆而下凌，則貳國之心叛矣。遠近由是而解體，奸雄以之而窺伺，舉動一失，大勢已去，晉之霸德至此掃地而無遺矣。《春秋》所以幸其功之著而惜其德之隳者，有由然也。吁！輕逞輙快者無大畧，堅
translation_en: … [Ma]sui. With the Di tribes submitting and Qin struck with fear, the worries in the northwest were laid to rest. Wu and Chu were locked in warfare, spreading poison among the various Ji-surname states, which threatened to divide our authority as hegemon. If this were not addressed, there would be no way to fulfill our duty. Thus, he grandly assembled the rulers of the states to establish relations with Wu at Zhongli, binding them to come together in agreement; he again reviewed the infantry and chariots to win a victory over Chu at Yanling, extinguishing the barbarian miasma. With Wu brought into peaceful alignment and Chu weakened, the anxieties in the southeast were dispelled. His renown swept rapidly from start to finish, and his martial strategy reverberated within and without. The four strong powers stepped back and heeded orders, external alarms subsided somewhat, and the progression of Jin's hegemonic achievements was on the whole impressive to behold. At this juncture, had he been cautious in cultivating his conduct and mindful of seeing things through to the end so as to win over those who came in allegiance, it might still have been promising! Yet Duke Li's ambitions did not lie in greatness, and an arrogant heart easily arose. Take a state that commanded popular esteem like Lu, which all the rulers looked up to: he ought to have drawn it close. If he rejected it, there would be no way to bind people's hearts. Yet at the meeting of Shasui, he accepted the slanders of Qiaoru [Shusun Xuanbo] and refused to grant an audience to our Duke [Duke Cheng of Lu], thereby severing friendly relations; and with the seizure at Tiaoqiu, he listened to the request of Xi Chou, making excessive demands on Jisun [Jisun Xingfu] to gratify his desires. With its ruler humiliated and its minister seized, our state of Lu became alienated at heart. Take a vacillating state like Zheng, upon which the rise and fall of hegemony depended: he ought to have conciliated it. If he treated it harshly, there would be no way to encourage the feudal lords. At first, in executing a punitive expedition, he led the various states to confront them in arms, with Yin [Count Wen of Yin] and Shan [Duke襄 of Shan] leading the vanguard; subsequently, in marching to attack again, he covenanted at Keling to send forth the army, humiliating the royal ministers a second time. By showing disrespect to his superior above and bullying his inferiors below, the hearts of the wavering states were driven to rebellion. Those far and near consequently fell apart, and ambitious schemers took advantage of this to watch for an opening. With a single misstep in his actions, the overall momentum was lost, and the hegemonic virtue of Jin was swept into the dust with nothing left. There is indeed a reason why the Spring and Autumn Annals is glad that his achievements were manifest yet laments that his virtue was ruined. Alas! Those who lightly indulge themselves and seek quick gratification lack grand strategy, whereas those who firmly…

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
恐持重者多遠圖夷考晉厲所為不越數端而心
術所存偹見惟負芻一討僅能得請命之正亦假
義飾舉者也他何觀焉求如晉悼之起四代之衰
復文襄之盛者惡可例論先儒謂悼公有君子之
資而厲無足稱也歟
禮記
主先嗇而祭司嗇也祭百種以報嗇也
毛憲
同考試官訓導林批此題作者多於祭百種報嗇
===
處講貫不明至有不知主配為何神者此作體認既明文
亦通暢宜寘優等
同考試官教諭朱批作此題者多昧本旨惟此篇發
明蜡祭報功之意殆盡宜表出之
考試官教諭趙批此篇說蜡禮祀神報功之意甚嘉
考試官教授戴批題本平易作者多欠切實詞簡
意盡僅見此篇
立索饗之神雖異報教穡之功則同夫先嗇司嗇
皆司百種而有功於農者先王立為主配而意深
punctuated:
恐持重者多遠圖。夷考晉厲所為，不越數端，而心術所存偹見。惟負芻一討，僅能得請命之正，亦假義飾舉者也，他何觀焉？求如晉悼之起四代之衰、復文襄之盛者，惡可例論？先儒謂「悼公有君子之資，而厲無足稱也」歟！

禮記

主先嗇而祭司嗇也，祭百種以報嗇也。

毛憲
同考試官訓導林批：此題作者多於「祭百種報嗇」處講貫不明，至有不知主、配為何神者。此作體認既明，文亦通暢，宜寘優等。
同考試官教諭朱批：作此題者多昧本旨，惟此篇發明蜡祭報功之意殆盡，宜表出之。
考試官教諭趙批：此篇說蜡禮祀神報功之意甚嘉。
考試官教授戴批：題本平易，作者多欠切實。詞簡意盡，僅見此篇。

立索饗之神雖異，報教穡之功則同。夫先嗇、司嗇，皆司百種而有功於農者。先王立為主、配，而意深
translation_en:
…patient and prudent have far-reaching plans. When we calmly examine the deeds of Duke Li of Jin (晉厲), they do not exceed a few instances, yet the inclinations of his heart and mind are fully revealed. Only in the single punitive expedition against Fuchu (負芻) did he barely manage to attain the correctness of requesting a mandate, and even that was merely borrowing righteousness to dress up his action; what else in him is worth looking at? If one seeks someone like Duke Dao of Jin (晉悼), who revived the decline of four generations and restored the flourishing of Dukes Wen and Xiang (文襄), how could they be discussed in the same breath? Is this not why earlier Confucians said, "Duke Dao had the qualities of a gentleman, whereas Duke Li is not worth mentioning"?

Record of Rites (Liji 禮記)

"It treats the First Husbandman (Xiansi 先嗇) as the principal deity and sacrifices to the Superintendent of Husbandry (Sisi 司嗇); it sacrifices to the spirits of the hundred grains in order to recompense husbandry."

Mao Xian 毛憲
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Lin: Most candidates writing on this topic failed to explain clearly the passage on "sacrificing to the hundred grains to recompense husbandry," to the point that some did not even know which deities were the principal and the coadjutor. This essay is clear in its comprehension and fluent in its prose; it should be placed in the superior grade.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zhu: Most of those who wrote on this topic were blind to its fundamental purport. Only this essay exhaustively elucidates the meaning of the year-end蜡 (Zha) sacrifice as a recompense for meritorious service; it should be singled out for distinction.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhao: This essay's explanation of the meaning of the Zha ritual in sacrificing to the spirits and recompensing merit is most admirable.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Dai: The topic is inherently plain and easy, yet most writers lacked concrete substance. Succinct in wording and exhaustive in meaning—that is seen only in this essay.

Although the deities established to be sought out and feasted are different, the recompense for the merit of teaching husbandry is the same. Now, the First Husbandman and the Superintendent of Husbandry both preside over the hundred grains and have rendered meritorious service to agriculture. The former kings established them as the principal deity and the coadjutor, and the intention behind their deep…

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之豈非報其教穡之功乎見於郊特牲之篇其旨
如此昔先王於歲終之時而舉行蜡祭之禮其所
立之神有主焉有配焉是故先嗇古之神農始為
耒耜以教民稼穡者也開物成務而有功於先故
祭必尊之為八神之主焉司嗇古之后稷播厥百
穀以教民樹藝者也謹司成法而有功於後故祭
必次之為先嗇之配焉夫主以先嗇非徼福也盖
以先嗇乃司百種之神而有教民稼穡之功故主
八神而祭之所以報其功也配以司嗇非求媚也
===
盖以司嗇乃司百穀之神而有教民樹藝之功故
配先嗇而祀之所以酬其功也吁舉蜡祭之禮盡
報功之道先王敬神重農之意不於斯而可見哉
雖然蜡之祭不特報先嗇司嗇而已若農郵表畷
坊與水庸貓虎昆蟲亦皆祭之而不遺焉夫合聚
萬物而饗之者非特八神也而所重者八神以其
尤有功於農故也其神之尊者非特先嗇也而所
主者先嗇以其始有事於農故也一蜡之中而禮
義周密如此伊耆氏始為蜡而後世行之也良有
punctuated: 之，豈非報其教穡之功乎？見於《郊特牲》之篇，其旨如此。昔先王於歲終之時而舉行蜡祭之禮，其所立之神，有主焉，有配焉。是故先嗇，古之神農，始為耒耜以教民稼穡者也。開物成務而有功於先，故祭必尊之為八神之主焉。司嗇，古之后稷，播厥百穀以教民樹藝者也。謹司成法而有功於後，故祭必次之為先嗇之配焉。夫主以先嗇，非徼福也，盖以先嗇乃司百種之神，而有教民稼穡之功，故主八神而祭之，所以報其功也。配以司嗇，非求媚也，盖以司嗇乃司百穀之神，而有教民樹藝之功，故配先嗇而祀之，所以酬其功也。吁！舉蜡祭之禮，盡報功之道，先王敬神重農之意，不於斯而可見哉？雖然，蜡之祭，不特報先嗇、司嗇而已，若農、郵表畷、坊與水庸、貓虎、昆蟲，亦皆祭之而不遺焉。夫合聚萬物而饗之者，非特八神也，而所重者八神，以其尤有功於農故也；其神之尊者，非特先嗇也，而所主者先嗇，以其始有事於農故也。一蜡之中，而禮義周密如此，伊耆氏始為蜡，而後世行之也，良有…
translation_en:
…them—is this not to repay their merit in teaching husbandry? As seen in the chapter "Single Victim at the Border Sacrifices" (Jiao te sheng), such is the purport.

In antiquity, at the end of the year, the former kings performed the rites of the Zha festival; among the deities they established, there was a principal deity and there was an associate deity. Therefore, the First Husbandman (Xianse)—the Divine Farmer (Shennong) of antiquity—was the one who first fashioned plows and plowshares to teach the people sowing and reaping. Because he initiated material undertakings and brought affairs to completion, having merit at the beginning, in the sacrifice he was necessarily honored as the principal among the eight deities. The Director of Husbandry (Sise)—Houji (Lord Millet) of antiquity—was the one who sowed the hundred grains to teach the people planting and cultivation. Because he carefully administered the established methods and had merit afterward, in the sacrifice he was necessarily ranked next as the associate to the First Husbandman. Now, making the First Husbandman the principal deity was not to seek blessings; rather, because the First Husbandman is the spirit in charge of the hundred seeds and had the merit of teaching the people sowing and reaping, they made him the principal of the eight deities and sacrificed to him in order to repay his merit. Making the Director of Husbandry the associate deity was not to curry favor; rather, because the Director of Husbandry is the spirit in charge of the hundred grains and had the merit of teaching the people planting and cultivation, they associated him with the First Husbandman and worshiped him in order to requite his merit. Ah! By performing the rites of the Zha sacrifice and exhausting the way of repaying merit, can the intention of the former kings in revering the spirits and valuing agriculture not be seen right here?

Even so, the Zha sacrifice did not merely repay the First Husbandman and the Director of Husbandry; others such as the Husbandmen (Nong), the Field-Huts and Boundary-Paths (Youbiaozhuo), the Dikes (Fang) and the Channels (Shuiyong), the Cats and Tigers (Maohu), and the Insects (Kunchong) were also all sacrificed to without omission. Now, in gathering together the myriad things to feast them, it was not only the eight deities, yet those given primacy were the eight deities because they had especial merit in agriculture; among the spirits that were honored, it was not only the First Husbandman, yet the one made principal was the First Husbandman because he first engaged in the work of agriculture. Within a single Zha festival, the ritual principles were as thorough and meticulous as this. That Divine Sovereign Yiqishi first instituted the Zha festival and later generations practiced it truly has…

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
六央
是故大人舉禮樂則天地將為昭焉天地訢合
陰陽相得煦嫗覆育萬物然後草木茂區萌
達羽翼奮角觡生蟄蟲昭蘇羽者嫗伏毛者
孕鬻胎生者不殰而卵生者不殀則樂之道
歸焉耳
謝遷
同考試官訓導林批此題本冠冕作者多分釋不明
此篇獨能融會成文發出聖人制作之功和氣生成之妙所
===
宜錄出
同考試官教諭朱批作此題者多泛冗可厭惟此篇
辭約而理不遺蓋深於禮者也尤宜高薦
考試官教諭趙批融會傳註成文敻然出乎眾作
考試官教授戴批禮樂之感大矣闚其奧者僅見
此篇
惟聖人制作以宣乎造化之妙故和氣生成而歸
於制作之功蓋大人制禮作樂將以昭宣天地化
育之道也則夫二氣和而萬物生成者孰非由於禮
punctuated:
六央。

是故大人舉禮樂，則天地將為昭焉。天地訢合，陰陽相得，煦嫗覆育萬物，然後草木茂，區萌達，羽翼奮，角觡生，蟄蟲昭蘇，羽者嫗伏，毛者孕鬻，胎生者不殰，而卵生者不殀，則樂之道歸焉耳。

謝遷。
同考試官訓導林批：此題本冠冕，作者多分釋不明；此篇獨能融會成文，發出聖人制作之功、和氣生成之妙，所宜錄出。
同考試官教諭朱批：作此題者，多泛冗可厭；惟此篇辭約而理不遺，蓋深於禮者也，尤宜高薦。
考試官教諭趙批：融會傳註成文，敻然出乎眾作。
考試官教授戴批：禮樂之感大矣，闚其奧者，僅見此篇。

惟聖人制作以宣乎造化之妙，故和氣生成而歸於制作之功。蓋大人制禮作樂，將以昭宣天地化育之道也；則夫二氣和而萬物生成者，孰非由於禮
translation_en:
…there is reason for it [? 六央, garbled for 以夫].

"Therefore, when the great man promotes rites and music, Heaven and Earth will be made manifest by them. Heaven and Earth unite in joy, yin and yang are in harmony, warming and brooding over, covering and nurturing the myriad things. Thereafter, grasses and trees flourish, bent sprouts break through, feathered wings stir, horns and antlers grow, hibernating insects awaken to life, feathered creatures brood over their eggs, furred creatures gestate and give birth, the womb-born do not miscarry, and the egg-born do not crack prematurely; all this is attributable to the Way of music."

Xie Qian 謝遷.
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Lin comments: This topic is inherently grand and dignified, yet most writers failed to analyze and explain it clearly. This essay alone manages to synthesize the ideas into a coherent composition, bringing forth the achievement of the sages' institution of rites and music and the marvel of harmonious qi generating and bringing things to completion. It ought to be selected for publication.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhu comments: Those who wrote on this topic were mostly vague, wordy, and tiresome. Only this essay is concise in expression yet leaves out none of the principles; indeed, the author is deeply versed in the Record of Rites, and especially deserves high recommendation.
Examiner, Instructor Zhao comments: Blending the commentaries and annotations into a unified composition, it stands far above the crowd of essays.
Examiner, Instructor Dai comments: Great indeed is the influence of rites and music! One who peers into their profound depths is seen only in this essay.

Because the sages instituted rites and music to manifest the marvel of the creative transformations of nature, the generation and completion of things through harmonious qi is attributable to the achievement of their institution. Indeed, when the great man institutes rites and creates music, it is in order to manifest and propagate the Way of the transforming nurture of Heaven and Earth; thus, when the two qi are in harmony and the myriad things are generated and brought to completion, how could any of this not be due to the…

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
樂參贊之功哉樂記載以示人宜矣且大人以至
聖之德居天子之位知禮樂順天地之情於是法
其序以制禮則三千三百秩如也法其和以作樂
則五聲六律純如也聖人制禮作樂豈徒然哉盖
以大哉乾元萬物資始將以是樂而昭宣之所謂
作樂以應天是已至哉坤元萬物資生將以是禮
而昭宣之所謂制禮以配地是已夫禮樂既舉則
天位乎上而氣下降至和交感而陰得乎陽地位
乎下而氣上騰太和流通而陽得乎陰天以氣煦
===
之而覆乎萬物地以形嫗之而育乎萬物由是植
物感其氣之和草木于焉而暢茂區萌于焉而條
達矣動物感其氣之和羽翼以之而奮起角觡以
之而發榮矣蟄藏之蟲感其和而初出如暗而得
明如死而更生焉羽為鳥屬羽者則體伏而生子
毛為獸屬毛者則姙孕而育子靡非和氣之所感
乎妊鬻為胎生而胎生者不至於殈體伏為卵生
而卵生者不至於殕靡非和氣之所形乎是則萬
物雖眾也皆得遂其生育之性庶類雖繁也悉得
punctuated: 樂參贊之功哉？《樂記》載以示人，宜矣。且大人以至聖之德，居天子之位，知禮樂順天地之情。於是法其序以制禮，則三千三百秩如也；法其和以作樂，則五聲六律純如也。聖人制禮作樂，豈徒然哉？盖以大哉乾元，萬物資始，將以是樂而昭宣之，所謂「作樂以應天」是已；至哉坤元，萬物資生，將以是禮而昭宣之，所謂「制禮以配地」是已。夫禮樂既舉，則天位乎上而氣下降，至和交感而陰得乎陽；地位乎下而氣上騰，太和流通而陽得乎陰。天以氣煦之而覆乎萬物，地以形嫗之而育乎萬物。由是植物感其氣之和，草木于焉而暢茂，區萌于焉而條達矣；動物感其氣之和，羽翼以之而奮起，角觡以之而發榮矣。蟄藏之蟲感其和而初出，如暗而得明，如死而更生焉。羽為鳥屬，羽者則體伏而生子；毛為獸屬，毛者則姙孕而育子，靡非和氣之所感乎？妊鬻為胎生，而胎生者不至於殈；體伏為卵生，而卵生者不至於殕，靡非和氣之所形乎？是則萬物雖眾也，皆得遂其生育之性；庶類雖繁也，悉得
translation_en:
…and music in assisting the cosmic transformations? It is fitting indeed that the Record of Music (Yueji) records this to instruct humanity.

Moreover, when the Great Man, possessing the virtue of the utmost sage, occupies the position of the Son of Heaven, he understands that rites and music accord with the dispositions of Heaven and Earth. Thereupon, modeling himself on their order, he institutes rites, so that the three thousand major and three hundred minor rules of ceremony are in perfect array; modeling himself on their harmony, he creates music, so that the five notes and six pitch-standards blend in pure unison. When the sage institutes rites and creates music, is it done in vain? Rather, because great is the originating power of Heaven (Qianyuan), from which the myriad things owe their beginning, he uses this music to manifest and proclaim it—this is what is meant by "creating music to respond to Heaven." And because supreme is the originating power of Earth (Kunyuan), from which the myriad things owe their birth, he uses these rites to manifest and proclaim it—this is what is meant by "instituting rites to match Earth."

Once rites and music are instituted, Heaven is positioned above while its vital energy descends, so that supreme harmony interacts and the yin receives the yang; Earth is positioned below while its vital energy ascends, so that great harmony circulates and the yang receives the yin. Heaven warms them with its vital energy and shelters the myriad things; Earth cherishes them with its physical form and nurtures the myriad things. Consequently, plants are moved by the harmony of this vital energy: grasses and trees thereby grow luxuriant, and hooked sprouts and buds thereby shoot forth and spread. Animals are moved by the harmony of this vital energy: winged creatures thereby rouse themselves to flight, and horned creatures—with antlers and horns—thereby flourish and thrive. Hibernating insects, moved by this harmony, emerge for the first time, as if passing from darkness into light, or as if dying and coming back to life. Feathered creatures belong to the category of birds, and feathered ones brood with their bodies to hatch their young; furred creatures belong to the category of beasts, and furred ones conceive and rear their young—is not all of this moved by the harmonious vital energy? Gestation and rearing constitute viviparous birth, and the viviparous do not suffer abortion; brooding with the body constitutes oviparous birth, and the oviparous do not end up with addled eggs—is not all of this given form by the harmonious vital energy?

Thus, although the myriad things are numerous, all are able to fulfill their nature of birth and growth; although the multitude of species are manifold, all are able to…

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
安其形色之天若此者豈無自而然哉要之一歸
於聖人禮樂叅賛之道耳向非聖人制禮作樂何
克以臻於斯雖然一氣未分禮樂在於天地兩儀
既闢禮樂在於聖人盖天地者禮樂之本原聖人
者禮樂之宗主非天地固無以肇禮樂之體非聖
人抑何以顯禮樂之用哉天地也聖人也禮樂也
相與流通而無間者歟操制作之柄者察諸
論
聖人神化上下與天地同流
===
童潮
同考試官訓導王批立意高行文富佳作也
同考試官訓導孫批議論疊出文勢洶湧
同考試官訓導吳批說有源流文有操縱
考試官教諭趙批豐贍可取
考試官教授戴批辭理通暢必佳士也
論曰大哉聖人乎其與天地同心而同功者
乎盖天地以生物為心而生生化化之功不
可以形容聖人以天地之心為心而施施化
punctuated:
安其形色之天。若此者，豈無自而然哉？要之，一歸於聖人禮樂叅賛之道耳。向非聖人制禮作樂，何克以臻於斯？雖然，一氣未分，禮樂在於天地；兩儀既闢，禮樂在於聖人。盖天地者，禮樂之本原；聖人者，禮樂之宗主。非天地固無以肇禮樂之體，非聖人抑何以顯禮樂之用哉？天地也，聖人也，禮樂也，相與流通而無間者歟！操制作之柄者察諸。

論
《聖人神化上下與天地同流》
童潮
同考試官訓導王批：立意高，行文富，佳作也。
同考試官訓導孫批：議論疊出，文勢洶湧。
同考試官訓導吳批：說有源流，文有操縱。
考試官教諭趙批：豐贍可取。
考試官教授戴批：辭理通暢，必佳士也。

論曰：大哉聖人乎！其與天地同心而同功者乎！盖天地以生物為心，而生生化化之功不可以形容；聖人以天地之心為心，而施施化
translation_en:
…rest secure in the natural endowment of their forms and colors. Could such a state come about without a cause? In sum, it all comes back to the sages' Way of participating in and assisting [the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth] through rites and music. Had the sages in the past not instituted rites and created music, how could things have reached this state? Even so, before the single vital energy divided, rites and music resided in Heaven and Earth; once the Two Modes [Heaven and Earth] were separated, rites and music resided in the sages. For Heaven and Earth are the fundamental source of rites and music, while the sages are the presiding masters of rites and music. Without Heaven and Earth, there would indeed be no way to initiate the substance of rites and music; without the sages, how then could the function of rites and music be made manifest? Heaven and Earth, the sages, and rites and music—do they not flow together without any gap! Let those who hold the authority to institute and create examine this.

Discourse
"The sage's spirit-like transformation flows together with Heaven and Earth above and below"
Tong Chao 童潮
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Wang: The conception is lofty and the writing rich; it is a fine piece.
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Sun: Arguments emerge one after another, and the momentum of the writing surges powerfully.
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Wu: The explanation traces back to its source and course, and the writing shows firm control in giving rein and holding back.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhao: Rich and ample; worthy of selection.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Dai: Both the diction and reasoning are fluent and clear; he must be a fine scholar.

The discourse states: Great indeed is the sage! Is he not one with Heaven and Earth in mind and in achievement! For Heaven and Earth take the generation of things as their mind, and their achievement of ceaseless generation and transformation cannot be described; the sage takes the mind of Heaven and Earth as his mind, and his achievement of extending and transforming…

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
化之功不可以窺測聖人也天地也其同一
太和元氣之流行也歟知此則程子所言之
㫖思過半矣或者乃曰莫大於天地之心非
德焉而心不相照莫大於天地之功非位焉
而功不相侔然則與天地同心而同功者其
惟有德有位之聖人乎彼帝如堯舜有是心
而有是功矣如孔子者祖述堯舜心則是矣
然位不堯不舜也功安在耶王如文武有是
心而有是功矣若孔子者憲章文武心則有
===
矣然位不文不武也功何在耶噫有是哉徒
觀聖人之已然而不觀夫聖人之必然難乎
與論聖人矣彼十年九水誰不知之苦於水
者曰天地無陽和也可乎不可乎八年七旱
誰不聞之苦於旱者曰天地無雨澤也可乎
不可乎孔子有德無位誰不惜之苦於無位
者曰聖人無神化也可乎不可乎盖善論聖
人者正不于其所已然而惟于其所必然也
是知孔子之神化上下與天地同流殆理之
punctuated:
化之功不可以窺測。聖人也，天地也，其同一太和元氣之流行也歟！知此，則程子所言之㫖，思過半矣。

或者乃曰：「莫大於天地之心，非德焉而心不相照；莫大於天地之功，非位焉而功不相侔。然則與天地同心而同功者，其惟有德有位之聖人乎！彼帝如堯、舜，有是心而有是功矣；如孔子者，祖述堯、舜，心則是矣，然位不堯不舜也，功安在耶？王如文、武，有是心而有是功矣；若孔子者，憲章文、武，心則有矣，然位不文不武也，功何在耶？」

噫！有是哉！徒觀聖人之已然，而不觀夫聖人之必然，難乎與論聖人矣。彼十年九水，誰不知之？苦於水者曰「天地無陽和也」，可乎不可乎？八年七旱，誰不聞之？苦於旱者曰「天地無雨澤也」，可乎不可乎？孔子有德無位，誰不惜之？苦於無位者曰「聖人無神化也」，可乎不可乎？盖善論聖人者，正不于其所已然，而惟于其所必然也。是知孔子之神化，上下與天地同流，殆理之
translation_en:
…transformation cannot be fathomed. The sage, along with Heaven and Earth—are they not the flowing forth of the very same supreme harmony and primordial vital energy (taihe yuanqi)? Once one understands this, one will have grasped more than half the purport of what Master Cheng said.

Someone, however, might say: "Nothing is greater than the mind of Heaven and Earth; without virtue, one's mind cannot correspond with it. Nothing is greater than the achievement of Heaven and Earth; without a ruling position, one's achievement cannot equal it. If so, then is it not only the sage who possesses both virtue and position whose mind and achievement are one with Heaven and Earth? Emperors like Yao and Shun possessed this mind and had this achievement; as for someone like Confucius, who transmitted the way of Yao and Shun, his mind was indeed right, yet his position was neither Yao's nor Shun's—where, then, was his achievement? Kings like Wen and Wu possessed this mind and had this achievement; as for someone like Confucius, who modeled himself on the regulations of Wen and Wu, he indeed had the mind, yet his position was neither Wen's nor Wu's—where, then, was his achievement?"

Alas! Can such a view be true? If one merely observes what actually came to pass for the sage, without observing what would necessarily have been so of the sage, it is difficult indeed to discuss the sage with such a person! That there were nine floods in ten years—who does not know of this? If those who suffered from the floods were to say, "Heaven and Earth have no warm yang harmony," would that be acceptable or not? That there were seven droughts in eight years—who has not heard of this? If those who suffered from the droughts were to say, "Heaven and Earth have no moistening rains," would that be acceptable or not? That Confucius possessed virtue without a ruling position—who does not lament this? If those troubled by his lack of position were to say, "The sage has no miraculous transformation," would that be acceptable or not? Indeed, one who is skilled at discussing the sage looks precisely not at what actually came to pass, but solely at what would necessarily have been so. Thus we know that Confucius's miraculous transformation, flowing above and below in concert with Heaven and Earth, is surely what principle…

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所必能者乎何則孔子之生形天地之塞也
清而明性天地之帥也純而粹朏cf大矣乎
一天地之包涵知識明矣乎一日月之照臨
至誠無息乎一四時之錯行隱顯莫測乎一
鬼神之潜伏觀其會相夾谷攝行相事神化
之胚胎成矣柰何一沮於女樂一簡於膰俎
沮之簡之者之過耳孔子何愧焉尼谿之封
書社之聘神化之萌蘖生矣柰何一惑於晏
嬰一沮於子西惑之沮之者之罪耳孔子何
===
尤焉致使東周之願不遂民無幸以際東周
耳於聖人何加損也周公之夢不復民無幸
以見周公耳於聖人何榮辱也設使天有意
於斯世斯民君師孔子焉九夷不必居也木
鐸孔子焉浮海不必歎也必將運天地大造
之心行天地至公之道秋陽以破天下之暗
江漢以濯天下之汙化雨不露于洙泗而露
乎天下之枯槁春風不播于杏壇而播乎天
下之慍懊立斯民也不寒而衣不饑而食而
punctuated: 所必能者乎！何則？孔子之生，形天地之塞也，清而明；性天地之帥也，純而粹。朏cf大矣乎，一天地之包涵；知識明矣乎，一日月之照臨；至誠無息乎，一四時之錯行；隱顯莫測乎，一鬼神之潜伏。觀其會相夾谷，攝行相事，神化之胚胎成矣。柰何一沮於女樂，一簡於膰俎？沮之、簡之者之過耳，孔子何愧焉！尼谿之封、書社之聘，神化之萌蘖生矣。柰何一惑於晏嬰，一沮於子西？惑之、沮之者之罪耳，孔子何尤焉！致使東周之願不遂，民無幸以際東周耳，於聖人何加損也？周公之夢不復，民無幸以見周公耳，於聖人何榮辱也？設使天有意於斯世斯民，君師孔子焉，九夷不必居也；木鐸孔子焉，浮海不必歎也。必將運天地大造之心，行天地至公之道，秋陽以破天下之暗，江漢以濯天下之汙；化雨不露于洙泗，而露乎天下之枯槁；春風不播于杏壇，而播乎天下之慍懊。立斯民也，不寒而衣，不饑而食，而
translation_en: … he would necessarily be capable of! Why is this so? At Confucius's birth, his physical form was that which fills Heaven and Earth—clear and bright; his human nature was that which directs Heaven and Earth—pure and unmixed. How vast was his bosom [? 朏cf], just like the all-embracing capacity of Heaven and Earth! How luminous was his knowledge, just like the shining down of the sun and moon! Was not his utmost sincerity unceasing, just like the alternating courses of the four seasons? Was not his hiddenness and manifestation unfathomable, just like the latent presence of ghosts and spirits? Observe how, when he served as assistant at the meeting at Jiagu and acted as Chief Minister, the embryo of his divine transformation was already formed. Yet what could be done when he was once thwarted by the female musicians and once slighted over the sacrificial meat? That was merely the fault of those who thwarted and slighted him; what shame was there for Confucius in that? With the proposed enfeoffment of the Nixi fields and the invitation with registered communities, the sprouts of his divine transformation had already sprung forth. Yet what could be done when one ruler was deluded by Yan Ying and another was thwarted by Zixi? That was merely the transgression of those who deluded and thwarted them; what blame was there for Confucius in that? That this caused his wish to create an "Eastern Zhou" to go unfulfilled meant only that the people had not the good fortune to encounter an Eastern Zhou; what did that add to or detract from the Sage? That his dreams of the Duke of Zhou did not return meant only that the people had not the good fortune to see the governance of the Duke of Zhou; what honor or disgrace was that to the Sage? Supposing that Heaven had had the intention to bless this world and this people, and had made Confucius their ruler and teacher, he would not have needed to speak of dwelling among the Nine Yi tribes; had it made Confucius its wooden-tongued bell, he would not have needed to sigh about floating out upon the sea. He would surely have operated with the mind of Heaven and Earth's great creation and practiced the Way of Heaven and Earth's utmost impartiality—bleaching with the autumn sun to dispel the darkness of All under Heaven, washing with the Jiang and Han rivers to cleanse the filth of All under Heaven. His transforming rain would not have moistened only the banks of the Zhu and Si rivers, but would have moistened the withered and parched throughout All under Heaven; his spring breeze would not have blown only over the Apricot Altar, but would have blown away the resentment and distress throughout All under Heaven. In establishing this people, they would be clothed before feeling cold and fed before feeling hungry, and…

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
相生相養者自忘於饑寒知其立而不知其
所以立矣道斯民也不刑而驅不勢而迫而
會極歸極者自忘於刑勢知其行而不知其
所以行矣立之未幾而綏以安之天地之栽
培不是厚也凡向之斯立者又將愛戴歸附
而捷於桴皷不啻雨露一潤而萬物濯濯然
聖人之神化豈不與天地同運而並行乎道
之未幾而動以振之天地之生成不是過也
凡向之斯行者又將於變時雍而捷於影響
===
不啻雷霆一鼓而萬物勃勃然聖人之神化
豈不與天地同旋而並轉乎禮樂不在周公
而在天下則大禮與天地同節大樂與天地
同和神化之見於禮樂者可見所以然者胡
可得而見耶賞罰不在春秋而在天下則五
服以彰天命五刑以用天討神化之見於刑
賞者可窺所以爾者胡可得而窺耶人徒知
天以神化覆物於上矣而不知聖人之神化
亦如天之無不覆幬也與天同流也為何如
punctuated: 相生相養者，自忘於饑寒，知其立而不知其所以立矣；道斯民也，不刑而驅，不勢而迫，而會極歸極者，自忘於刑勢，知其行而不知其所以行矣。立之未幾，而綏以安之，天地之栽培不是厚也。凡向之斯立者，又將愛戴歸附，而捷於桴皷，不啻雨露一潤而萬物濯濯然，聖人之神化豈不與天地同運而並行乎？道之未幾，而動以振之，天地之生成不是過也。凡向之斯行者，又將於變時雍，而捷於影響，不啻雷霆一鼓而萬物勃勃然，聖人之神化豈不與天地同旋而並轉乎？禮樂不在周公而在天下，則大禮與天地同節，大樂與天地同和，神化之見於禮樂者可見，所以然者胡可得而見耶？賞罰不在《春秋》而在天下，則五服以彰天命，五刑以用天討，神化之見於刑賞者可窺，所以爾者胡可得而窺耶？人徒知天以神化覆物於上矣，而不知聖人之神化亦如天之無不覆幬也，與天同流也為何如？
translation_en: … those who mutually sustain and nourish one another naturally forget about hunger and cold; they know that they are established, yet do not know whereby they are established. In guiding these people, they are driven without punishments and compelled without coercion, and those who converge upon the supreme standard and return to the supreme standard naturally forget about punishments and coercion; they know that they advance, yet do not know whereby they advance. Not long after establishing them, he pacifies and gives them peace—even the nurturing of Heaven and Earth is no more generous than this. All those who were previously thus established will furthermore love, revere, and turn to him in allegiance more swiftly than drumstick answers drum, just as when rain and dew once moisten, the myriad things gleam with vitality. Does not the marvelous transformation of the sage operate in unison and advance side by side with Heaven and Earth? Not long after guiding them, he stirs and rouses them—even the generation and completion of Heaven and Earth do not surpass this. All those who previously thus advanced will furthermore be transformed into universal harmony more swiftly than shadow follows form or echo follows sound, just as when thunder and lightning once rouse, the myriad things burst forth in vigor. Does not the marvelous transformation of the sage revolve in unison and turn side by side with Heaven and Earth? When rites and music reside not merely in the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong) but throughout the empire, then great rites share the same regulation as Heaven and Earth, and great music shares the same harmony as Heaven and Earth; the marvelous transformation manifested in rites and music can be seen, yet how could that whereby it is so be seen? When rewards and punishments reside not merely in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) but throughout the empire, then the five ceremonial vestments manifest the Mandate of Heaven, and the five punishments execute the chastisement of Heaven; the marvelous transformation manifested in punishments and rewards can be glimpsed, yet how could that whereby it is thus be glimpsed? People merely know that Heaven covers all things from above through its marvelous transformation, yet they do not know that the marvelous transformation of the sage is also like Heaven in leaving nothing uncovered. How great is its flowing in unison with Heaven! …

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
人徒知地以神化載物於下矣而不知聖人
之神化亦如地之無不持載也與地同流也
又何如迨見朞月而可三年有成皆不托之
空言上律天時下襲水土無不見之實事變
春秋之世為堯舜之世斯世無不以孔子尊孔
子而以堯舜尊孔子斯世皆從游也豈但三
千而已乎變春秋之民為文武之民斯民不
以夫子親夫子而以文武親夫子斯民皆速
肖也豈但七十而已乎明良康衢之歌不歌
===
堯舜而歌孔子雖至沒世而不忘焉聖人之
神化何間於存亡哉騶虞麟趾之詠不詠文
武而詠孔子雖終身而不忘焉聖人之神化
何分於久近哉夫聖人之神化如此所謂與
天地合德者在此與日月合明者在此與四
時合序與鬼神合吉凶亦在此矣大哉聖人
之神化無一不以彌綸天地而無間乎論而至
是則知非聖人與天地同心固無以同天地
神化之功非程子與子貢同心抑孰能名聖
punctuated: 人徒知地以神化載物於下矣，而不知聖人之神化亦如地之無不持載也，與地同流也又何如？迨見朞月而可，三年有成，皆不托之空言；上律天時，下襲水土，無不見之實事。變春秋之世為堯舜之世，斯世無不以孔子尊孔子，而以堯舜尊孔子，斯世皆從游也，豈但三千而已乎？變春秋之民為文武之民，斯民不以夫子親夫子，而以文武親夫子，斯民皆速肖也，豈但七十而已乎？明良康衢之歌，不歌堯舜而歌孔子，雖至沒世而不忘焉，聖人之神化何間於存亡哉？騶虞麟趾之詠，不詠文武而詠孔子，雖終身而不忘焉，聖人之神化何分於久近哉？夫聖人之神化如此，所謂與天地合德者在此，與日月合明者在此，與四時合序、與鬼神合吉凶亦在此矣。大哉聖人之神化，無一不以彌綸天地而無間乎！論而至是，則知非聖人與天地同心，固無以同天地神化之功；非程子與子貢同心，抑孰能名聖…
translation_en: People merely know that Earth through its wondrous transformation supports all things below, yet they do not know that the sage's wondrous transformation is likewise like the Earth in leaving nothing unsupported—how is it with flowing in harmony with Earth as well? One would then see that "in a year something could be done, and in three years there would be accomplishment" would none of it be consigned to empty words; "above, conforming to the seasons of Heaven, and below, adapting to the water and soil" would in every case be manifested in actual affairs. Transforming the age of the Spring and Autumn into the age of Yao and Shun, this age would without exception honor Confucius not merely as Confucius, but honor Confucius as Yao and Shun; the whole of this age would follow in his company—how could it be merely three thousand disciples and no more? Transforming the people of the Spring and Autumn into the people of King Wen and King Wu, these people would feel affection for the Master not merely as the Master, but feel affection for the Master as King Wen and King Wu; all these people would swiftly pattern themselves after him—how could it be merely seventy disciples and no more? The songs of the "Enlightened Ruler and Worthy Ministers" and of the "Highroad" would not be sung of Yao and Shun, but sung of Confucius, and even after his passing they would not forget him—how could the sage's wondrous transformation be divided by life and death? The chants of "Zouyu" and "Linzhi" would not be chanted of King Wen and King Wu, but chanted of Confucius, and to the end of their lives they would not forget him—how could the sage's wondrous transformation be distinguished by long or short duration? Now, the sage's wondrous transformation being such as this, what is called "uniting with Heaven and Earth in virtue" lies here; "uniting with the sun and moon in brilliance" lies here; "uniting with the four seasons in order, and uniting with ghosts and spirits in good and ill fortune" also lies here. Great indeed is the wondrous transformation of the sage—is there anything in which it does not encompass and weave together Heaven and Earth without the slightest gap! Reasoning to this point, one knows that unless the sage shares the same mind as Heaven and Earth, there is truly no way to share in Heaven and Earth's achievement of wondrous transformation; and unless Master Cheng shares the same mind as Zigong, who indeed could give name to the sage's…

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
人神化之妙乎雖然寧使聖人有神化無
邦家不可使聖人有邦家而無神化使孔子
誠得邦家不過堯焉舜焉而已文焉武焉而
已千萬世之下帝王孰為之師表人物孰為
之儀刑哉是以孔子不得邦家雖春秋之不
幸實千萬世之幸也觀其刪詩書定禮樂贊
周易脩春秋所以為天地立心為生民立命
為往聖繼絕學為萬世開太平而神化之妙
豈不與天地同流於悠久乎吁孔子往矣求
===
其下上與天地同流者今幸有
聖天子在上謹論
表
擬宋以陳堯叟同知樞密院事謝表
謝暹
同考試官訓導林批駢麗可觀
同考試官教諭朱批表佳
考試官教諭趙批表典雅
考試官教授戴批表得體
punctuated:
人神化之妙乎？雖然，寧使聖人有神化、無邦家，不可使聖人有邦家而無神化。使孔子誠得邦家，不過堯焉、舜焉而已，文焉、武焉而已，千萬世之下，帝王孰為之師表？人物孰為之儀刑哉？是以孔子不得邦家，雖春秋之不幸，實千萬世之幸也。觀其刪《詩》、《書》，定《禮》、《樂》，贊《周易》，脩《春秋》，所以為天地立心，為生民立命，為往聖繼絕學，為萬世開太平，而神化之妙，豈不與天地同流於悠久乎？吁！孔子往矣，求其下上與天地同流者，今幸有聖天子在上。謹論。

表
擬宋以陳堯叟同知樞密院事謝表
謝暹
同考試官訓導林批：駢麗可觀。
同考試官教諭朱批：表佳。
考試官教諭趙批：表典雅。
考試官教授戴批：表得體。
translation_en:
… the marvelousness of the sage's divine transformation? Even so, it is better for the sage to possess divine transformation without a state or clan than to possess a state or clan without divine transformation. Had Confucius truly gained a state or clan, he would have been no more than another Yao or Shun, no more than another King Wen or King Wu; down through ten thousand generations, who then would have served as the teacher and standard for emperors and kings, and who would have served as the model and pattern for humanity? Therefore, that Confucius did not gain a state or clan, though a misfortune for the Spring and Autumn era, was truly a fortune for ten thousand generations. Observe how he pared the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu), settled the Rites (Li) and Music (Yue), wrote commentaries on the Book of Changes (Zhouyi), and compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)—whereby he established the mind for Heaven and Earth, established the destiny for the living people, carried on the lost learning for past sages, and opened up great peace for ten thousand generations. Does not the marvelousness of his divine transformation flow together with Heaven and Earth in enduring perpetuity? Alas! Confucius is gone; yet in seeking one who flows together with Heaven and Earth above and below, today we are fortunate to have our Sacred Son of Heaven on high. Humbly discoursed.

Memorial (biao)
An Imitation of a Song-Dynasty Memorial by Chen Yaosou Giving Thanks for His Appointment as Co-administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs
Xie Xian
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Lin: The parallel prose is ornate and worth reading.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhu: A fine memorial.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhao: The memorial is classic and elegant.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Dai: The memorial is fitting in style.

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
伏以
宥省尊嚴近接
清光之地樞謨靖密宜資治世之才
綸音遽進於崇階朽質實艱於負荷望非意及
榮與憂并伏念〔臣堯叟〕僻處遐方叨逢
盛世芹宮脫迹僭登虎榜之名
楓陛傳臚曽沐鳳池之寵首登史館繼判度支
兩路撫安沐金紫輝煌之錫三班進職兼銀
臺封駁之權雖任使之荐更實勤勞之罕著
===
自虞隕墜誤被超遷俾參機要之司翊贊兵
戎之務捫心知愧揣分奚堪兹蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇德邁禹湯聖同堯舜
聰明睿知同日月之照臨
慈愛寬仁配乾坤之廣大臣民胥戴夷夏同歸
翕受敷施有寸長而必錄兼收並蓄雖片善
而不遺遂令樗櫟之才謬玷樞機之任權侔
台府位應斗杓敢不勉策駑庸上酬
鴻造皷三軍惰歸之氣大振
punctuated: 伏以宥省尊嚴，近接清光之地；樞謨靖密，宜資治世之才。綸音遽進於崇階，朽質實艱於負荷，望非意及，榮與憂并。伏念〔臣堯叟〕僻處遐方，叨逢盛世。芹宮脫迹，僭登虎榜之名；楓陛傳臚，曽沐鳳池之寵。首登史館，繼判度支。兩路撫安，沐金紫輝煌之錫；三班進職，兼銀臺封駁之權。雖任使之荐更，實勤勞之罕著。自虞隕墜，誤被超遷，俾參機要之司，翊贊兵戎之務。捫心知愧，揣分奚堪？兹蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇德邁禹、湯，聖同堯、舜。聰明睿知，同日月之照臨；慈愛寬仁，配乾坤之廣大。臣民胥戴，夷夏同歸。翕受敷施，有寸長而必錄；兼收並蓄，雖片善而不遺。遂令樗櫟之才，謬玷樞機之任。權侔台府，位應斗杓。敢不勉策駑庸，上酬鴻造；皷三軍惰歸之氣，大振
translation_en:
Humbly I consider: the Bureau of Military Affairs is august and solemn, a place in close proximity to the pure radiance of the throne; its pivotal counsels are quiet and confidential, and properly rely upon talents capable of governing the world. When the imperial voice suddenly advances me to a lofty rank, my decayed substance truly finds it difficult to bear the load; the expectation was beyond what my thoughts reached, and honor is joined with anxiety.

Humbly I reflect that [your servant Yaosou] dwelt in seclusion in a distant region, and undeservedly encountered a flourishing age. Leaving my tracks behind in the local school, I presumptuously ascended to a name on the "Tiger Placard" of successful candidates; when the roll was called at the Maple Steps of the palace, I was graced with the favor of the Phoenix Pool. First I ascended to the Historiography Institute, and subsequently served as Supervisor of the Bureau of General Accounts. Pacifying Two Circuits, I was bathed in the resplendent bestowal of the gold seal and purple ribbon; advancing in office in the Three Ranks of palace attendants, I concurrently held the Silver Terrace's authority to return imperial decrees for reconsideration. Although my commissions and assignments have repeatedly changed, in truth my diligent service has rarely been manifest. While I myself feared falling into ruin, I mistakenly received rapid promotion, causing me to participate in the agency of confidential affairs and to assist in the business of military matters. Laying my hand on my heart, I know shame; measuring my lot, how can I bear it?

This has come about because I have humbly encountered [Your Majesty, whose] virtue surpasses that of Yu and Tang, and whose sageliness equals that of Yao and Shun. Your intelligence, perspicacity, and farsightedness are like the shining down of the sun and moon; Your compassion, love, tolerance, and benevolence match the vastness of Heaven and Earth. Officials and people all revere You, and non-Chinese and Chinese alike turn to You in allegiance. Receiving broadly and applying widely, if someone has an inch of merit You unfailingly record it; gathering and storing all together, even a fragment of goodness You do not overlook. Thus You have caused a talent as useless as ailanthus and scrub oak to erroneously blemish a post at the pivot of state affairs, with authority equal to the Three Ducal Ministries and a position corresponding to the handle of the Northern Dipper. How could I dare not strive to spur on my dull mediocrity to repay on high Your vast creation; to rouse the flagging spirit of the Three Armies and greatly stir…

title: 成化十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
國威運萬全決勝之謀仰資
廟筭伏願
一人有慶同山嶽之奠安
萬壽無疆竝天地之悠久臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉表稱
謝以
聞
策
===
第一問
謝遷
同考試官訓導林批治教一策學者多不知其詳是
篇發明無滯其熟於策學者歟
考試官教諭趙批隨問隨荅不為問目所窘策手也
考試官教授戴批敷陳詳盡文理明暢策之尤者也
對前聖建繼天立極之功而道所由行後聖
成垂世立教之典而道所由明夫莫為於前
雖美不彰莫為於後雖善不傳所謂先聖後
punctuated:
國威，運萬全決勝之謀，仰資廟筭。伏願一人有慶，同山嶽之奠安；萬壽無疆，竝天地之悠久。臣無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

策

第一問
謝遷
同考試官訓導林批：治教一策，學者多不知其詳，是篇發明無滯，其熟於策學者歟！
考試官教諭趙批：隨問隨荅，不為問目所窘，策手也。
考試官教授戴批：敷陳詳盡，文理明暢，策之尤者也。

對：前聖建繼天立極之功，而道所由行；後聖成垂世立教之典，而道所由明。夫莫為於前，雖美不彰；莫為於後，雖善不傳。所謂「先聖後…
translation_en:
…the majesty of the state, and devise all-encompassing strategies that guarantee victory to reverently assist the imperial court's planning. I humbly wish that the One Man may enjoy blessings, as firmly established as the great mountains, and that his myriad years of longevity may be boundless, as enduring as Heaven and Earth. Your servant is overwhelmed with the utmost gratitude and trepidation as he gazes up toward Heaven and looks up to the Sage, and respectfully presents this memorial of thanks for Your Majesty's information.

Policy Essays (Ce)

First Question
By Xie Qian 謝遷
